title: Checkpoint 6: Magnus vs Stockfish (skill 0)
notes: Checkpoint after game 6, from the Italian Game: Magnus plays the yardstick, Stockfish at skill 0. Nothing is studied afterwards.

moves.thought: This is the main-line Giuoco Piano and 5.d4 is the principled central break, hitting the e5 pawn and the c5 bishop; I checked the greedy tries first — Nxe5 Nxe5 and Bxf7+ Kxf7 both just drop a piece. After 5.d4 exd4 6.cxd4 Bb4+ the only check is harmless (Bd2 or Nc3 blocks and I keep a strong centre), and no Qh4 ideas exist with my knight on f3 guarded.

Recapturing with the pawn is the main line: 6.cxd4 builds the big centre, and Black can't take on d4 (6...Bxd4 7.Nxd4 Nxd4 8.Qxd4 wins a piece) nor grab 6...Nxe4 because 7.d5 traps the knight and forks my pieces back. Nxd4 instead would surrender the centre after 6...Nxd4 7.Qxd4 d6, and 6.e5 runs into 6...d5 hitting my bishop, so the pawn recapture is clearly best.

Black's 6...Bb6 was exactly the move I once punished with 7.e5, hitting the f6 knight and gaining the d-file/central space; after 7.e5 Ne4 8.Bd5 the knight on e4 has no pawn support and c6 is hit too, while 7...Nxe5 8.dxe5 wins a piece. None of my pieces are loose and Black has no check available right now.

Black's Ng4 is unsupported and my king is still safe, so I checked the tactic first: 8.Bxf7+ Kxf7 9.Ng5+ forks the king and the loose g4 knight, and after any king move 10.Qxg4 nets a pawn plus Black's castling rights (bishop traded for knight+pawn). Declining with 8...Kf8 just leaves me a clean extra pawn after the bishop retreats.

My bishop on f7 is attacked by the king, so it must retreat with purpose; Bd5 is safe (no pawn can chase it since ...c6 is blocked by the knight), hits Nc6 and the g8 square, and keeps the loose Ng4 under pressure for h3. I checked Black's tries: 9...Nxf2 10.Kxf2 Qh4+ 11.g3 Qxd4+ 12.Be3 Qxd5 13.Qxd5, 9...Nxd4 10.Nxd4 Bxd4 11.Qxg4, and 9...Ncxe5 10.dxe5 Ngxe5 11.Nxe5 all leave me clearly ahead in material, and Black has no checks.

My d5 bishop is attacked by the knight on b4, and Bxb7 just loses it to Bxb7, while Be6/Bf7/Bg8/Bc6 all drop it to Bxe6, Kxf7, Rxg8 or dxc6; Bc4 is met by ...d5 (since Nb4 also covers d5), so the one retreat that is both safe and pawn-proof is Bb3, defended by a2 and immune to ...d5. After Bb3 I keep the a2-g8 diagonal aimed at the exposed king, and tries like ...Nxf2 Kxf2 simply leave Black a piece down.

Black's knight on g4 is loose and unsupported, so 11.h3 kicks it with tempo — Nxf2 or Nxe5 just loses a piece (f2: Kxf2 and Bxd4+ is met by Be3; e5: Nxe3... Nxe5 recaptures since Nf3 guards it), Nxh2 fails to Nxh2/Rxh2, and ...Nh6 invites Bxh6 gxh6 shattering Black's kingside. I checked every Black check: Nd3+ and Nc2+ drop the knight to Qxd3/Qxc2, and ...Qh4 is not check with my f2 pawn home and simply loses the queen to Nxh4.

Black's loose knights (b4, h6) give him no real threats: Bxd4 fails to Nxd4 Qxd4 Qxd4, Nd3 or Nc2 drops to Qxd3/Bxc2 since my Bb3 guards c2 and Ra1 guards a2, so I can safely tuck my king away while staying a pawn up. Castling removes any e1-h4 check tricks (my rule 1) and connects my rooks before developing the queenside; after O-O ...Ng4 hxg4 hxg4 ...Qh4 I simply answer Nh2/Ne1 and the queen sortie costs Black material.

I'm a pawn up with Black's king stuck on f8 and his bishop/knight passive, so I want a tempo-gaining space move rather than a quiet one: 13.d5 hits the c6 knight and the pawn is safely guarded by Bb3, so 13...Nb4 14.a3 drives the knight to the rim, and 13...Nb4 14...Nbxd5/Nxa2 both just lose a piece to Bxd5 or Rxa2. I checked Black has no checks and no sound capture (13...Nxd4 and 13...Nxe5 both drop material to Nxd4/dxe5), and my f2/g2 squares stay covered by Rf1 and the king if the queen tries Qh4.

The d5 push attacks the e7 knight and is only guarded by the c7 pawn, so 14.d6 cxd6 15.exd6 recaptures and plants a permanent wedge that hits e7 and c7 again, keeps Bc8/Ra8 bottled up and the king stuck on f8, with my queen on d1 guarding d6 so ...Nf5xd6 is impossible. I rejected 14.e6 because dxe6 dxe6 Qxd1 liquidates my extra pawn and frees Black's bishop, and 14.Bxh6 just trades my good bishop and opens the g-file. Black's only check, ...Bxf2+, simply loses a bishop to Rxf2.

Bg5 hits the queen on d8 along the d8–g5 diagonal, and I verified the counter-capture: Qxg5 fails to Nxg5 since my knight on f3 guards the square (queen for bishop in my favour). Black's queen has only e8 (e7 loses to dxe7+, f6 to Bxf6), so I gain a tempo, keep my strong d6 wedge instead of cashing it with dxc7, and avoid g4 which simply drops the pawn after hxg4 hxg4 Nxg4 with Black's rook on the open h-file.

Black's queen on d8 is defended only by the knight on f7 (the c8-bishop can't guard along the rank and Bb6's diagonal is blocked by the c7 pawn), so Bxd8 Nxd8 wins queen for bishop, a clean +6 material swing. I verified Black has no intervening check or counter-capture that changes the count.

I'm a whole queen up after 16.Bxd8, so my priority is to rescue that bishop from the d8 corner and simplify; Bxb6 trades my bishop for Black's active dark-squared bishop (which eyes f2) and after axb6 Black has no checks or counterplay. I rejected Be7+ because Nf5xe7 just wins the piece back.

I'm already up a queen for nothing, so I want a safe, simplifying move that also grabs material: Qd3 hits the completely undefended knight on f5 (nothing black has covers d3 — the c8 bishop is boxed in by b7/d7, and Nf5/Nf7 don't reach it), while keeping Nf3 guarding e5 and the b6/b3 bishops untouchable.

I'm a full queen up, but I spotted that my bishop on b6 is actually hanging to ...axb6, so I must resolve it now — and Bxa7 both saves the bishop and wins the pawn while hitting the undefended rook on b8. After 19...Ra8 the bishop simply retreats to b6/d4 (no black checks or captures exist: ...Nxe5 just drops a knight to Nxe5), leaving me a queen and two pawns ahead.

Black's rook on b8 is completely undefended — the bishop on c8 doesn't cover b8 and the h8 rook's path along the eighth rank is blocked by the king on f8 — so Ba7xb8 simply wins a whole rook. Black has no checks and no counter-captures (Nxe5 is met by Nxe5 or Qxe5), so this is clean material on top of my already overwhelming advantage.

I'm up a queen and a rook, so I just need safe, risk-free consolidation: Nxh4 grabs the loose h-pawn, since h4 is defended by nothing (Nh6 covers g4/f5/f7/g8, not h4) and Black has no checks or counter-captures that win anything — ...Nxe5 just drops the knight to Qd4. I avoided Be6 (Bxe6) and Bd5 (cxd5), and my Bb8 still has a7/c7 to retreat to.

I'm already up a queen, rook and bishop, so the cleanest path is simplification: Bxg8 wins the rook, and the only recapture is Kxg8, leaving me a bishop-for-rook richer with no counterplay (…Nxh3+ just drops a knight to gxh3). My pieces stay mutually safe and no black check or capture hits anything loose.

My bishop on g8 is attacked by Nh6 and the king, so I must deal with it; Bxe6 only trades it off, while Bh7 is attacked by nothing (Nh6 covers g8/f7/f5/g4, not h7) and keeps me a whole extra bishop with escape squares g6/f5/e4 if the king or ...g6 comes after it. Black's knights on e6 and h6 are both loose, so after Bh7 I can pick one up or punish ...Nf4 with Qg3 while staying totally winning.

My Nh4 is attacked by the new g5 pawn, so I need a move that saves it; Ng6+ hops out with check and lands on a square guarded by my Bh7, where neither black knight (Nh6 covers g8/f7/f5/g4, Ne6 covers g7/g5/f4) can touch it. I checked Qf5+ loses the queen to Nxf5, and all my other pieces (Qd3, Bb8, both rooks) are unattacked after the check.

I'm up a queen and two rooks' worth of material, so my priority is consolidating loose points rather than grabbing more: I noticed d6 is completely undefended and Black's ideas are ...Nhf5 hitting d6 and ...Nf4 hitting my queen. Rd1 develops my last inactive rook, guards d6 along the file, and leaves nothing of mine capturable (Black has no checks or captures at all after it).

Black's bishop on c8 is completely boxed in by its own b7/d7 pawns and has no defenders, and my d6 pawn guards e7, so Ne7 cannot be met by Kxe7 or any knight capture and threatens the unstoppable Nxc8. I checked Black has no checks or counter-tactics: if gxh3 I simply recapture gxh3 and still take the bishop, keeping my overwhelming material edge.

Black's ...g3 just pokes at f2, but it costs nothing serious since fxg3 or Kxf2 are always available, and no black piece defends c8. Counting captures, Nxc8 snaps off the bishop for free (nothing attacks or recaptures on c8, and the knight retains retreats via a7/b6/e7), leaving me a queen, two rooks and three pieces up; after ...gxf2+ Kxf2 any ...Nf4 is simply met by Qxf4.

Black's only counterplay is the g3 pawn plus Ng4 hitting f2 (note gxf2+ would stop Kxf2 while the knight guards it), so I remove the knight with tempo: hxg4 is a free piece since nothing recaptures on g4, and afterwards gxf2+ Kxf2 or gxh2+ Kxh2 is completely harmless.

I'm overwhelmingly ahead (queen, two rooks, two bishops, two knights vs. a lone knight), so my only job is to remove Black's lone source of counterplay — the g3 pawn — while keeping every piece safe. Qxg3 grabs it with nothing attacking g3, keeps my f2/g2 pawns intact and guarded by the king, and if Black tries ...Nf4 I simply take it with Qxf4+; Black has no checks at all.

My bishop on h7 is loose and attacked by the black king (Kxh7), so it must move; Bg6 and Bg8 are also king-attacked and undefended, so the only retreat that is both pawn-supported (by g4) and gains a tempo is Bf5, which attacks the e6 knight. If Black answers Nd4xf5, gxf5 recaptures and I remain overwhelmingly ahead in material.

I'm overwhelmingly ahead in material (queen, two rooks, two bishops, two knights against a lone knight), so the cleanest path is to eliminate Black's only piece: Bxe6 is met solely by dxe6, leaving Black with just a king and three pawns against my whole army. Simplifying matches my rule about welcoming trades when far ahead, and I verified no counter-captures or checks exist for Black afterwards.

Black is down to a bare king and three pawns, so I just need a clean mating net without hanging anything (Ne7 would drop the knight to ...Kf8). Pushing g5 gives the pawn control of f6 and h6, so after a follow-up Qh3/Qh4 the queen lands on h6 with pawn support and it's mate, since Be6 already covers f7 and g8.

I'm overwhelmingly ahead (Black has only king and three pawns), so I looked for the fastest forced mate: with Be6 covering f7/g8, the e5 and g5 pawns covering f6, and the g5 pawn guarding h6, a queen landing on h6 is mate against the king on g7. Qh4 threatens Qh6#, and the only try ...Kg6 runs into Qh5+ Kg7 Qh6#; nothing attacks h4, and Black still has ...b5/...c3 so there's no stalemate risk.

With a huge material lead my only concern is Black's c-pawn running (c3 then cxb2 hitting my a1 rook) and putting my queen on a square the king can take — so I rejected Qh7+/Qh8+ (Kxh7/Kxh8) and Rd5/Rd4-type moves near the e6 pawn. Qxc4 is completely safe (nothing defends c4 and Black's king is far away), removes his only real counterplay, and leaves my loose bishop and knight untouchable.

I'm overwhelmingly ahead, so I want the safest forcing path rather than a flashy queen move; d7 is completely unstoppable (nothing attacks d7 or the d8 square) and gives me a second queen next move. Black's only replies are harmless king shuffles or ...b4, and there's no check, capture or stalemate trick available to him.

Black has only a king and two pawns, so the cleanest path is to promote; d8 is completely undefended (the king is on g7 and nothing covers d8), so d8=Q is a free second queen with no recapture. I checked it isn't stalemate — Black still has Kg6, Kf7, Kh7 and ...b3 — and my own king is perfectly safe.

Black has only a king on g7 and a b3 pawn, so there are no checks or captures to fear; Qxe6 grabs the free pawn (e6 is undefended since the king can't reach it) while building a mating net — Qd8 covers f8/g8/h8, g5 covers h6/f6, and Qe6 covers f7/g6/g8. Then 38.Qf7# follows after ...Kh7, and after ...b2 I have 38.Qf6+ Kh7 39.Qf7#; black still has pawn moves so there's no stalemate trick.
Black has only a king on h7 and a b3 pawn, and 38.Qf7 is mate — the queen covers g8, g6 and h7 along the rank, g5 pawn guards h6, and my other queen on d8 covers h8.
